chunks: What al-Shaykh informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥujr ibn Zāʾidah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever deliberately leaves [unwashed] a hair in the ghusl of janābah, then he is in the Fire."

Then he said—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: ghusl is with one sāʿ of water, and its measure is nine Baghdādī ratls; that is complete thoroughness, and less than that is sufficient for tahārah. Thus, this indicates that.

key_terms.إِسْبَاغٌ: full and thorough completion of washing
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, indicating severe punishment in the afterlife
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a measured quantity of water used here as a standard amount for ghusl

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about leaving part of the body unwashed in ghusl al-janābah?
ai.summary: This report stresses the necessity of thorough ghusl from janābah and warns against deliberately leaving any part of the body, even a single hair, unwashed. It also notes that one sāʿ of water represents complete and ample washing, while a lesser amount may still suffice for valid ritual purification.
